records.deidentified_narrative: on [date] at approximately 19:46 i chief mark birchard thorndale police department, milam county texas was dispatched to an [roadway] 79 and fm 486. police responded to investigate. upon arrival i was advised of a hispanic male that was crossing at or in [roadway] 79 and fm 486, [roadway] 79 traffic per witnesses and vehicle driver, which meant the pedestrian was crossing against the light, and that the pedestrian was looking down while walking. the pedestrain was later identified at aurelio soto garcia hm [date] no dl or id card located. the driver of the vehicle that struck garca stated he was at the posted speed limit of 45 mph driving east towards rockdale and as he entered the intersection did not see garcia until it was too late to stop in time. the driver identified as ronald rabinowitz wm dob [date] tx dl 38751553 was driving a silver chevrolet equinox bearing tx lp [identifier] occupied by rabinowitz and front passenger seat was his wife pam warren. garcia was struck by the suv and fell on the front of the hood, he layed there until about 30 feet later as rabinowitz stopped the suv, garcia fell off the hood onto the shoulder of the roadway. rabinowitz exited the vehicle and attempted to render aid, other witnesses stopped and reported that garcia was crossing against the light, and looking down. appeared to never see the oncoming suv. witnesses id'd as:david castillo jr hm [date] tx dl 37390765 of rockdalejohn paul erman wm [date] tx dl 37313809 of rockdaletrooper luna offered to assist with a forensic diagram to be updated later. paint marks were applied to vehicle locationa and patient location for later measuring. amr ems arrived along with thorndale fd and medical assistance was provided for garcia. the medical helicopter was requested and a landing zone lz was established by the fire department, who also provided traffic control so the police units could work the accident. prior to the helicopter arrival ems moved garcia into the ambulance to package him for transport. at some point garcia coded and cpr was begun. the helicopter landed and air medics assisted the other ems personel. after working the patient for 40 plus minutes or more the decision was made to cease cpr. the ambulance and helicopter both have protocols that will not allow them to transport an active cpr code. jp 4 gary northcott was dispatched to pronounce.

records.deidentified_narrative: on september 13th, 2020, around 9:15 pm, i, trooper clopton, was called to a two-vehicle crash on us 281 near mp [roadway]. this area of us 281 is not lighted. unit 1 was traveling northbound on us 281 near the scotland city limit sign. unit 2 was parked on [roadway] of travel of us 281. unit 2 was approximately 1-2 car lengths south of a large green texas department of transportation scotland city limit roadway sign. the sign is made with reflective material, which makes it visible at night. i believe unit 2 had become disabled due to mechanical issues. unit 2's emergency brake was engaged with the keys out of the ignition. unit 2 trunk lid was in the open position during the time of the crash. all the reflective rear brake light housing was visible on the vehicle. it was not impacted by the truck being open. i also observed what i believe to be an auto part in the front passenger seat of unit 2. i spoke with a friend of jones. the friend stated that unit 2 was always having mechanical issues and breaking down. the friend noted every time jones came to visit him. he had to fix something on unit 2. jones, the driver of unit 2 was outside his vehicle near the passenger side trunk area. based on my experiences and the physical evidence on the two units and the condition of jones body, i believe jones was either bent over inside the trunk or could have seen unit 1 approaching and jumped inside the trunk in an attempt to save himself with his legs partially outside the vehicle. unit 1 [roadway] [roadway], and drove on the improved shoulder when prohibited and struck jones and unit 2s rd with its fd. after the impact, unit 2 spun slightly over 180 degrees and came to rest upright facing southeast onto the center strip divider of us 281. in my opinion, i believe, jones was thrown from the truck area of unit 2 after the impact into the grass ditch on the east side of the roadway. jones was then run over with the driver side tires of unit 1. jones came to rest facing south approximately 5 [roadway]. jones sustained catastrophic injuries to his legs approximately mid-thigh and down. after the impact unit 1 swerved to the right, entered the grass ditch on the east side of us 281. unit 1 ran over jones with its driver-side tires. unit 1 continued in the grass ditch and struck a t-post and a barb wire fence before coming rest against a tree approximately 10-25 yards inside the fence line. after the impact unit 1, the front right tire became pinched between the fender and the bumper of unit 1. i believe this caused the tire to lock up somewhat, which caused the vehicle to pull partially to the right. due to the odor of alcohol coming from unit 1, sfsts were conducted on the driver of unit 1. the driver showed no signs or indication of intoxication. trooper sorge and i spoke with the driver of unit 1 and could not observe or smell any alcohol odor coming from his breath or persons. i talked to the driver of unit 1, and he informed me that he was going home and was listening to music on his cell phone. according to the driver, his phone was linked to the units radio via blue tooth. i spoke with the driver, and he stated that he was singing. he also said when he looked up, he was already on top of unit 2, and it was too late. in my opinion, i believe the driver of unit 1 had some form of distraction within the vehicle while driving either by singing or utilizing his cell phone for music. in another interview with the driver of unit 1, he informed me that when he left scotland en-route to his parents in windthorst approximately one and a half hours earlier, he did not observe unit 2 or any other vehicle on the shoulder. in my opinion, i believe unit 2 was parked on [roadway] of travel. jones, the driver of unit 2, had his keys on his person. i observed the manual transmission in what i believe was in the neutral position with the emergency brake engaged. based on my experiences, if jones was pushing the vehicle off the roadway, the key probably should have been in the ignition so he could steer the vehicle, and the emergency brake disengaged. based on these factors and the physical evidence left on the roadway from the impact area, i do not believe unit 2 [roadway] impeding traffic or [roadway]. the pedestrian's toxicology results were obtained from the autopsy report.

traveling northbound on us 281 near the scotland city limit sign. unit 2 was parked on [roadway] of travel of us 281. unit 2 was approximately 1-2 car lengths south of a large green texas department of transportation scotland city limit roadway sign. the sign is made with reflective material, which makes it visible at night. i believe unit 2 had become disabled due to mechanical issues. unit 2's emergency brake was engaged with the keys out of the ignition. unit 2 trunk lid was in the open position during the time of the crash. all the reflective rear brake light housing was visible on the vehicle. it was not impacted by the truck being open. i also observed what i believe to be an auto part in the front passenger seat of unit 2. i spoke with a friend of jones. the friend stated that unit 2 was always having mechanical issues and breaking down. the friend noted every time jones came to visit him. he had to fix something on unit 2. jones, the driver of unit 2 was outside his vehicle near the passenger side trunk area. based on my experiences and the physical evidence on the two units and the condition of jones body, i believe jones was either bent over inside the trunk or could have seen unit 1 approaching and jumped inside the trunk in an attempt to save himself with his legs partially outside the vehicle. unit 1 [roadway] [roadway], and drove on the improved shoulder when prohibited and struck jones and unit 2s rd with its fd. after the impact, unit 2 spun slightly over 180 degrees and came to rest upright facing southeast onto the center strip divider of us 281. in my opinion, i believe, jones was thrown from the truck area of unit 2 after the impact into the grass ditch on the east side of the roadway. jones was then run over with the driver side tires of unit 1. jones came to rest facing south approximately 5 [roadway]. jones sustained catastrophic injuries to his legs approximately mid-thigh and down. after the impact unit 1 swerved to the right, entered the grass ditch on the east side of us 281. unit 1 ran over jones with its driver-side tires. unit 1 continued in the grass ditch and struck a t-post and a barb wire fence before coming rest against a tree approximately 10-25 yards inside the fence line. after the impact unit 1, the front right tire became pinched between the fender and the bumper of unit 1. i believe this caused the tire to lock up somewhat, which caused the vehicle to pull partially to the right. due to the odor of alcohol coming from unit 1, sfsts were conducted on the driver of unit 1. the driver showed no signs or indication of intoxication. trooper sorge and i spoke with the driver of unit 1 and could not observe or smell any alcohol odor coming from his breath or persons. i talked to the driver of unit 1, and he informed me that he was going home and was listening to music on his cell phone. according to the driver, his phone was linked to the units radio via blue tooth. i spoke with the driver, and he stated that he was singing. he also said when he looked up, he was already on top of unit 2, and it was too late. in my opinion, i believe the driver of unit 1 had some form of distraction within the vehicle while driving either by singing or utilizing his cell phone for music. in another interview with the driver of unit 1, he informed me that when he left scotland en-route to his parents in windthorst approximately one and a half hours earlier, he did not observe unit 2 or any other vehicle on the shoulder. in my opinion, i believe unit 2 was parked on [roadway] of travel. jones, the driver of unit 2, had his keys on his person. i observed the manual transmission in what i believe was in the neutral position with the emergency brake engaged. based on my experiences, if jones was pushing the vehicle off the roadway, the key probably should have been in the ignition so he could steer the vehicle, and the emergency brake disengaged. based on these factors and the physical evidence left on the roadway from the impact area, i do not believe unit 2 [roadway] impeding traffic or [roadway]. the pedestrian's toxicology results were obtained from the autopsy report.

records.public_safe_text: i made the location for a call of a major accident involving a pedestrian. when i arrived to the location ems was already treating ped in their vehicle. ped was conscious and [roadway] rash. ped's foot was beginning to swell showing a potentially broken leg. ped told me that he was just walking southbound on the grass to the side of roosevelt. ped stated that he looked back and saw unit 1 swerve into him and hit him. at this point ped was transported to sammc with non-life threatening injuries. i spoke with w1 who was driving behind unit 1. w1 stated that she was driving behind unit 1 and he just began to lose control. w1 stated that unit 1 swerved to [roadway] and hit the guardrail and then continued [roadway] to the right. w1 saw unit 1 hit ped, and unit 1 immediately stopped. i released w1 at the scene and went to speak with the operator of unit 1. the operator of unit 1 stated that he was just driving southbound on roosevelt when he lost control of his vehicle. he stated that he attempted to regain control but overcorrected and went into the guardrail. the operator of unit 1 stated that [roadway] and didn't see ped until the last second. unit 1 stated that he hit ped and immediately tried to slow down to check on him. the operator of unit 1 appeared to be alert and in control of his normal faculties. i did not notice any odor of intoxicants on the operator of unit 1. i conducted hgn on the operator of unit 1 but observed no signs of intoxication. i called for a tow truck for unit 1 and when the contract tow arrived unit 1 was towed to growdon. the operator of unit 1 was issued a citation for operating his motor vehicle without insurance and released at the scene. i left the scene without further incident. coban/bwc available.

records.deidentified_narrative: the operator of unit 1 was driving northwest out of the parking lot when she stopped to talk to a person driving away. the operator stopped unit 1, exited the vehicle, and walked around the front right of the vehicle. the operator then started walking west back to the driver side of unit 1. while stopped, unit 1 began to roll northwest. the operator did not see the unit rolling as she walked in front of it, and was struck by its front and rolled over by one of its wheels. by checking the function of the gear shift, i learned the vehicle's transmission was partially non functional. the reverse gear did not catch and the park was only set with a firm upward pull on the gear shift. i determined the operator's failure to set brakes was the primary contributing factor, and the vehicle's poor state of repair may have contributed to the accident by causing the vehicle to slip out of park while stopped and idling. see hcso investigative report 2010-02546. supplement 10. 22. 20: txdot corrected this report by separating the operator of unit 1 from unit 1, making her unit 2 (pedestrian) because she was out of the vehicle when the crash happened.

records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 was traveling east on ih 10 [roadway]. a pedestrian walked north west into the lanes of travel from the eastbound barrow ditch, attempting to cross ih 10. the pedestrian further failed to yield right of way to unit 1. unit 1 struck [roadway]. unit 1 came to rest upright [roadway]. the pedestrian came to rest face down in [roadway]. it is believed the pedestrian was looking for help after recently being involved in a one vehicle crash. at the location of where the crash occurred, there is a gas station located across ih 10 (on the north side). upon taking inventory of the pedestrian's vehicle that was located approximately 0. 5 miles southwest of the scene, several syringes were discovered as well as on his person. the toxicology results from the autopsy revealed the pedestrian was positive for eutylone (synthetic stimulant), alprazolam (xanax), and benzoylecgonine (main metabolite of cocaine).
